requirement:
When the backend and model support prompt caching, every provider request MUST
place one cache checkpoint after the system prompt of
{cite}`requirements.authoring.prompt_parts` and another at the end of its last
message, so each request reuses the tool definitions and system prompt that
earlier assessments of its kind sent, and the conversation its own earlier
requests sent. Cache checkpoints MUST NOT change the content of a request.
rationale:
I found no gap against `requirements.authoring.cache_checkpoints`.

**Obligations**
1. **Checkpoints on every request when backend and model support caching.**
   - `RigProvider::connect` (`src/authoring/providers.rs:112`) sets `caches`. For Bedrock it calls `bedrock_caches(model)`, which is true for the Claude and Nova families via `rig_bedrock::completion::Family::of`. For Ollama it is false, because Ollama has no prompt-cache checkpoints.
   - `CompletionProvider::complete` (line 188) runs for every request. When `self.caches` is set it calls `place_cache_checkpoints`.
   - `place_cache_checkpoints` (line 330) sets `request.options.cache = Some(CacheRetention::Short)`.
   - Per its doc comment, the vendored `rig-bedrock` then emits `cachePoint` blocks after the system prompt and at the end of the last message. I did not read the vendored implementation. The integration test below checks this on the wire.
2. **One checkpoint after the system prompt and another at the end of the last message.** The integration test `claude_requests_carry_cache_checkpoints_and_record_cache_usage` (`tests/authoring_cli.rs:1826`) runs a Claude model against a fake Bedrock endpoint and asserts four things on both requests:
   - `system` has two entries, the text and then a `cachePoint`.
   - The last content block of the last message is a `cachePoint`.
   - There are exactly two `cachePoint` occurrences in each body.
   - The second request, which follows a reasoning turn, still ends in a checkpoint.
3. **Checkpoints MUST NOT change the content of a request.**
   - The unit test `cache_checkpoints_are_requested_for_caching_models` (`src/authoring/providers.rs:600`) asserts that only `options.cache` differs after `place_cache_checkpoints`.
   - The integration test strips `cachePoint` blocks from the cached bodies with `without_cache_points`. It asserts they equal the bodies sent to a non-caching model.
4. **Only supported models get checkpoints.** The unit test asserts `bedrock_caches` is true for Claude and Nova models and false for Llama and an unknown fixture model. The integration test confirms that a non-caching model's request has no `cachePoint`.

The requirement cites `prompt_parts` only for what "the system prompt" means, so I did not reassess it. I found no unspecified behavior in the `impl` code and no `{fixme}` references.

text: When the backend and model support prompt caching, every provider request MUST
place one cache checkpoint after the system prompt of
{cite}`requirements.authoring.prompt_parts` and another at the end of its last
message, so each request reuses the tool definitions and system prompt that
earlier assessments of its kind sent, and the conversation its own earlier
requests sent. Cache checkpoints MUST NOT change the content of a request.
Each assessment conversation MUST send its prompt as a system prompt followed by
one user message, the subject message, filled from the first and second text
blocks of the prompt requirement for the assessment's kind. The kinds are
requirement, example, citation review, site review, and a verifier of each of
those. A system prompt MUST be the same for every assessment of its kind, so
every placeholder whose value depends on the subject MUST be in the subject
